item.title: Show HN: SlopIt - A blog your coding agent runs (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
Hi HN! This is something I built out of my own need. I'm doing several projects on the side, and many of them need a CMS quickly (automated by my agents), and I thought there's space for a very minimal thing that's more agent-native instead of setting up the heavy blogging platforms.

A few things that stand out here - you, as a human, cannot post or update your content. You need to tell your agent to do it. It's designed like this on purpose because that's where the industry is going.

Although it's named SlopIt a bit tongue-in-cheek, obviously not trying to encourage actual slop here - I think if done the right way, LLM-assisted writing could be as good as human writing (and will only get better over time).

Some of the example blogs I've setup for my projects: - https://blog.rafikigo.com/why-we-started-rafikigo/ (Blog for a Kenyan tour company) - https://blog.simbastack.com/ (Blog for my consulting firm)

I'd love for you guys to try it out and provide feedback.

--

Getting started is super simple - just copy the prompt (shown in the Hero) and drop it into your agent and you have a new blog ready.

I do recommend spending some time and effort in using Skills and projects like Humanizer (https://github.com/blader/humanizer) to make your content more readable for humans.

Oh and the core is open source (MIT) - https://github.com/Simbastack-hq/SlopIt

item.title: Show HN: Cryo - A language whose programs live forever (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
Cryo is a programming language that models long-running tasks like workflows or AI agents. Programs freeze to disk when idle and can be thawed when new data arrives.

As part of our announcement of Endothermic Labs, we've put together a small demo of Cryo that highlights its features and walks through the language and its plugin system.

We originally built it as a way to deploy healthcare agents at scale, but have rebuilt it from the ground up to be a standalone toolchain for long-running tasks. It acts as something like a cross between Durable Objects and Temporal workflows, where the script itself is the durable unit with no replay needed.

Cryo is statically and structurally typed, with a concurrency model similar to Go. It's still under active development, so we're holding off on open sourcing it until we're confident that the language is stable, ideally in the next 3-4 weeks.

item.title: Show HN: Open Dataset of the Lebanese Law (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
Hey folks! I made it easier for builders to use the lebanese legislation through: a public DB, API, and MCP.

The Lebanese University has an archive of all laws dating back to 1904 (legallaw.ul.edu.lb). People and AI can barely find it and navigate it. It also had outdated articles.

Now, more people are using it. Builders for their startups, lawyers for their work, and students for their bar prep. I'm still trying to get it trusted by authorities.

The database includes the edges between every law, article, ruling and Gazette issue. You can easily identify how they influence one another.

Articles are versioned, so you can see how it was affected by other laws from the date it was published.

100k unofficial english translations were added using LLMs. They aren't accurate, but they help with search and SEO/AEO/GEO. We're working on producing legally accurate translations.

47k rulings were PDFs, some handwritten. We converted all of them to text using OCR, flagging handwritten files. We're working on an HTR model specifically for those to increase the confidence.

Today, other datasets in Lebanon charge for this data. I'm doing it as a public service. I want change in my country. And, lately, I think it's through helping builders. Yet, what I'm doing is legally wrong, but hopefully morally acceptable.
